====== CONTEXT 1 — Divider ======

====== CONTEXT 2 — It started in your field ====== For a neuroscience audience: the idea of artificial neural networks came from neuroscience. Keep it to two minutes; the point is the lineage. Definitions (say them only if asked): - Artificial neuron (McCulloch & Pitts): a unit that adds up its weighted inputs and "fires" (outputs 1) when the sum passes a threshold. - Perceptron (Rosenblatt): one layer of such units whose weights are LEARNED from labelled examples: wrong answer → nudge the weights. - Neural network (multi-layer): layers of units, every connection a weight; the hidden layers build intermediate features the output layer combines. - Hopfield network: a recurrent network in which memories are stable states (energy minima) the network settles into. - Backpropagation: computes how much each weight contributed to the error and adjusts all weights, layer by layer, from the output backwards. - Deep learning: neural networks with many layers, trained on large data with GPUs. Sources: McCulloch & Pitts 1943 (Bull. Math. Biophys.); Rosenblatt 1958; Hopfield 1982 (PNAS); Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams 1986 (Nature); Krizhevsky, Sutskever & Hinton 2012 (AlexNet); Nobel Prize in Physics 2024. Diagrams: drawn for this deck.

====== CONTEXT 3 — From next word to agents ====== Definitions: - Token: a piece of text, a word or part of a word ("neur" + "on"). - Parameter (weight): a number learned in training; GPT-3 has 175 billion. - Transformer: the architecture behind every modern language model: a stack of layers, each with self-attention and a feed-forward network; processes all tokens of a text in parallel. - Self-attention: lets every token weigh every other token when building its representation ("it" looks back at "neuron"). - GPT: "generative pre-trained transformer". - Reasoning model: trained to work through intermediate steps before answering. - Coding agent: a language model in a loop with tools (files, terminal, tests). Sources: Vaswani et al. 2017 "Attention is all you need"; Brown et al. 2020 (GPT-3, 175 billion parameters); GitHub Copilot preview June 2021; ChatGPT 30 Nov 2022; OpenAI o1, Sept 2024; Claude Code (Feb 2025 preview) and OpenAI Codex (2025); Karpathy coins "vibe coding", Feb 2025.

====== CONTEXT 4 — How an LLM works ====== Walk through the five steps on the diagram. Then the four consequences: fluent is not the same as true; it only knows its training data; it only "sees" what fits in its context window; the same question can give different answers (step 4 picks among probabilities).

====== CONTEXT 10 — At the frontier ====== Diagrams drawn for this deck, describing how each system works. - AlphaFold 2 (Jumper et al., Nature 2021): predicts a protein's 3-D structure from its amino-acid sequence, with a per-residue confidence score (pLDDT, colours as in the AlphaFold database). Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2024 (Hassabis, Jumper; with Baker for protein design). Not a language model, but the same deep-learning family. - AI co-scientist (Google, Feb 2025): several agents generate, review, debate, rank in a tournament and refine hypotheses for a scientist's goal. - The AI Scientist (Lu et al., Sakana AI, 2024, arXiv 2408.06292): automates idea → code and experiments → paper → automated review, end to end. Its papers were of mixed quality.
